passage: The wedding hall was loud, and the photographer had only a few minutes left before the family portrait. Uncle after uncle came over. "Jagdish, top of the class again!" "Such a bright boy!" Aunties pinched his cheek. At the edge of the crowd, his sister Preeti stood holding her plate, unseen. Jagdish's face went hot. He could see her smile fading. He didn't want to be the golden boy if it meant this. "Excuse me, Aunty." He walked over and took her hand. "Preeti, come stand at the front with me. You made those flowers on the stage, remember?" "Really?" she whispered. "Really." He told the photographer, "Please make space for my sister," and put her beside him instead of behind.

qa.q: What did Preeti make for the stage, according to Jagdish?
qa.a: She made the flowers on the stage.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling when the relatives praised him while Preeti stood unseen?
qa.a: He felt guilty and uncomfortable, and did not want to be the favourite if it meant leaving his sister out.

qa.q: What did Jagdish do to include Preeti without competing for approval?
qa.a: He took her hand, named something she had done, and asked the photographer to make room for her at the front.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt when Jagdish came over?
qa.a: Probably relieved and a little surprised to be noticed, since she'd been unseen and her smile was fading.

grounding: Shows a golden-child teen feeling guilty as his sister is overlooked, refusing to compete and gently including her.
